 Karl-Anthony Towns provides candid answer to returning to Timberwolves question
 Karl-Anthony Towns had a candid answer when asked about his first game against Minnesota since winning the title with the Knicks.
 By Rishabh Bhatnagar • Nov 19, 2026 at 3:13 PM ET • 2 min read Add ClutchPoints on Google Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images The Minnesota Timberwolves host Karl-Anthony Towns and the New York Knicks for the first time since they won the championship last season on Thursday night at the Target Center. KAT, who spent nine seasons with the Timberwolves after being selected by the franchise as the No. 1 pick of the 2015 draft, described the experience as bittersweet.
 The 31-year-old claimed that he wanted to win a championship for Minnesota, calling the city his home, per a post on X by Jared Schwartz.
 Expand Tweet 
 “Great to be home and to be back here,” he said. “Nine years of my life, some amazing years, amazing moments. Yeah, it’s special to be back. Obviously I am taking off a day, it’s bittersweet, to come back with a championship because, you know, I wanted to win it here so bad for the city, for Minneapolis, for Minnesota, for all the people who haven’t seen the championship here.”
 Towns went on to explain that he was using the time to see his friends, describing them as ‘family,’ and explained that he was out eating at his favorite spots. Towns was traded to the Knicks in October 2024, but not before he had made a mark at his former franchise.
 Article Continues Below KAT left ranking second behind Kevin Garnett in over a dozen major Timberwolves franchise records, including points, rebounds, and blocks. And while there was limited postseason success during his time, Towns undoubtedly still sees the franchise as his home.
 Regardless, the Knicks will take on the surging Timberwolves without star man Anthony Edwards , although Minnesota have gone 8-3 in his absence. Both teams arrive to the game looking to extend their winning streak to three, although Minnesota still have a number of players on the injury list.
 The Knicks, meanwhile, are healthier, and have not listed a single name on the official injury list before this game.
